pr.title: Refactor AddCallGuards in two loops.
pr.description:
This PR splits the pass into an analysis loop and a change loop. This allows to avoid invalidating CFG caches if there are no changes to be performed.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR is a pure performance refactor of `AddCallGuards` that produces an identical MIR body. The only behavioral difference described is that the pre-PR version always calls `body.basic_blocks_mut()`/`extend(new_blocks)` even when `work` is empty, invalidating CFG caches; with empty `new_blocks`, the body contents are unchanged. Similarly, splitting mutation into a separate loop changes only mutation timing, not the computed destinations, guard blocks, source_info, is_cleanup, or `cur_len + new_blocks.len()` indices. CFG-cache invalidation is not observable in a normal Rust program's numeric/boolean/character values, and the refactored pass's output MIR is exactly equal for every input, including empty-work, critical Call, and InlineAsm cases. There is therefore no source-grounded pair of ordinary Rust functions whose original and "transformed" values differ on concrete inputs; constructing one would require fabricating an unrelated semantic change not justified by the PR.

analysis.originalLogic: AddCallGuards breaks outgoing critical edges for call terminators in MIR. It first counts predecessors for every basic block (`pred_count`). It then examines each block's terminator: a `TerminatorKind::Call` with `target: Some(destination)` is broken when `pred_count[destination] > 1 && (generates_invoke(unwind) || self == &AllCallEdges)`. In `CriticalCallEdges` mode, `TerminatorKind::InlineAsm { asm_macro: InlineAsmMacro::Asm, .. }` is handled when it `has_outputs` (InOut/Out) and `(has_labels || generates_invoke(unwind))`; each target with `pred_count[target] > 1` is broken. Breaking an edge means replacing the target with a newly created `BasicBlockData::new(Some(Terminator { source_info, kind: TerminatorKind::Goto { target } }), is_cleanup)`. New blocks are appended after the original body length, using `let idx = cur_len + new_blocks.len();`, where `cur_len = body.basic_blocks.len()`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical implementation performed analysis and mutation in one mutable loop: `for block in body.basic_blocks_mut()` and immediately assigned `*destination = new_block(...)` / `*target = new_block(...)`. Consequently it always took mutable access to the CFG and always extended the body, even when no critical edge matched, unnecessarily invalidating CFG caches. The PR replaces this with an immutable analysis loop over `body.basic_blocks.iter_enumerated()` that records `(bb, Action::Call)` or `(bb, Action::Asm { target_index })` in `work`, followed by `if work.is_empty() {` / `return;` and a separate mutation loop using `body.basic_blocks.as_mut()`. The transformation must preserve the exact edge-breaking predicate and new-block index scheme; only mutation timing and the empty-work early return change.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies passed to the AddCallGuards `MirPass`, including bodies with no critical call/asm edges (empty `work`), `Call` terminators with `target: Some(_)` and either invoke-generating or non-invoke unwind depending on pass mode, and `InlineAsm` terminators containing outputs, labels, unwind, and multiple target entries with varying predecessor counts. Two programs can differ only by whether any terminator satisfies the edge-breaking predicate, exercising the empty-work early return.
analysis.summary: AddCallGuards was refactored from a single mutable CFG walk into an immutable analysis loop plus a deferred mutation loop, with an empty-`work` early return. This is a performance optimization: it avoids taking mutable CFG access and invalidating CFG caches when no critical edges need breaking, while preserving the exact edge-breaking predicates, new-block append indices, and cleanup/source-info propagation.
analysis.trigger: Running AddCallGuards over a MIR body where no outgoing critical edge needs to be broken, i.e. the collected `work` list is empty. The pre-PR code still entered `body.basic_blocks_mut()` and extended the body, invalidating CFG caches; the refactor returns early instead. The same trigger also covers mode-dependent matching: `AllCallEdges` versus `CriticalCallEdges`, and `InlineAsm` requiring outputs plus labels or invoke unwind.
preconditions: Compute `pred_count` from all basic block terminators before deciding which edges are critical.
For Call: break only when `target: Some(destination)`, `pred_count[destination] > 1`, and `generates_invoke(unwind) || self == &AllCallEdges`.

For InlineAsm: only in `CriticalCallEdges` mode with `asm_macro: InlineAsmMacro::Asm`, and only when there are output operands (`InOut` or `Out`) and either label operands or invoke-generating unwind.
For each InlineAsm target independently, break only when `pred_count[target] > 1`.
Create replacement blocks as `Goto { target }` with the original terminator's `source_info` and the source block's `is_cleanup`.
Append new blocks after the original body length: capture `cur_len = body.basic_blocks.len()` and use `cur_len + new_blocks.len()` for each new BasicBlock index.
pitfalls: The empty-work early return must occur before any mutable CFG access (`body.basic_blocks.as_mut()` / `basic_blocks_mut()`); otherwise the cache-invalidation optimization is lost.
Do not re-evaluate `pred_count` after mutation or process newly inserted Goto blocks; they are single-predecessor guards and must not themselves be broken.
The analysis loop must not mutate terminators while reading them; the `work` entries rely on the terminator shape remaining unchanged until the mutation loop.

`Action::Asm { target_index }` indexes the original asm `targets` array. The mutation loop must re-index the same array (`&mut targets[target_index]`) after the immutable analysis loop, not a copied or reordered target list.
New block indices must be based on the original body length captured before extension; appending first or recomputing length after some blocks are added would produce wrong target blocks.
Preserve `source_info` from the terminator and `is_cleanup` from the source block when creating guard blocks.
The refactor moves the `debug!("Broke {} N edges", ...)` logging after the empty-work check, so the zero-edge case no longer emits that debug message; this is diagnostic-only, not a semantic change.
`Simplify CFG` can undo this pass's edge breaking, so tests should check the immediate post-pass CFG rather than a later simplified CFG.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-level rustc tests that build inputs differing only in whether any edge is critical. (1) No-critical-edge case: a Call with a single predecessor (or InlineAsm without qualifying outputs/labels/unwind) should leave the CFG unchanged and exercise the empty-`work` early return. (2) Critical Call case: a Call whose target has `pred_count > 1` with invoke-generating unwind (or `AllCallEdges` mode) should gain a new Goto guard block; verify the Call target now points to the appended block and that the guard Goto points to the original destination, with matching `source_info` and `is_cleanup`. (3) InlineAsm case in `CriticalCallEdges` mode with outputs and labels/unwind and multiple targets: only target indices whose predecessors exceed one should be replaced, each with its own new Goto block. (4) Verify exact BasicBlock numbering (`cur_len + new_blocks.len()` order) and that multiple guarded targets on one terminator all update correctly. (5) Check `AddCallGuards` idempotence: running it again should produce no further critical edges, and no new blocks when none are needed. Include a case where the pass does perform work to confirm the early return does not skip required edge breaking. The supplied patch contains no regression-test hunks, so these tests must be constructed.
evidence: This PR splits the pass into an analysis loop and a change loop. This allows to avoid invalidating CFG caches if there are no changes to be performed.
Breaks outgoing critical edges for call terminators in the MIR.
NOTE: Simplify CFG will happily undo most of the work this pass does.
